title: Remote Windows service creation through SC
description: Detects sc.exe commands that target a remote Windows host and request creation of a service.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary with administrative credentials may create a service on a remote Windows host to execute a payload with elevated privileges or maintain persistence.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents SC's UNC server target and create operation, and MITRE describes sc.exe service creation as a persistence and privilege-escalation mechanism; enterprise administration can use the same interface.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify sc.exe commands that combine a remote UNC target with the service create operation while leaving local creation, remote queries and other remote service actions unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Identify the source and target hosts, service configuration and supplied binary path, then validate the activity against an approved remote-administration workflow.
steps: Review the complete SC command, source device, account, remote target, service name, binary path and parent process.
Inspect the target for service installation, start activity, dropped payloads, network logons and execution under SYSTEM.
Confirm an approved deployment or support change with the responsible owner; remove the service, isolate affected hosts and rotate exposed credentials when unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved remote software deployment, support and service administration through SC

validation.expected_outcome: Match remote service-create commands through SC; do not match local creation, remote query or delete actions, or another process carrying similar text.
